title_en: Interim Regulations on the Management of Carbon Emission Rights Trading

articles.content_en:
Article 7 Key greenhouse gas emitting entities included in the national carbon emissions trading market (hereinafter referred to as key emitting entities) and other entities that meet the relevant provisions of the State may participate in carbon emissions trading.
Staff members of the competent department of ecological environment, other departments with supervisory and management responsibilities for carbon emissions trading and related activities (hereinafter collectively referred to as other departments with supervisory and management responsibilities), the national carbon emissions registration institution, the national carbon emissions trading institution, and technical service institutions as specified in these Regulations shall not participate in carbon emissions trading.

Article 8 The competent department of ecological environment under the State Council shall, together with the relevant departments under the State Council, formulate the conditions for determining key emitting entities in accordance with the national greenhouse gas emission control targets. The competent department of ecological environment of the people's government of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government (hereinafter collectively referred to as the provincial people's government) shall, together with the relevant departments at the same level, formulate the annual list of key emitting entities in its administrative region in accordance with the conditions for determining key emitting entities.
The conditions for determining key emitting entities and the annual list of key emitting entities shall be disclosed to the public.

Article 9 The competent department of ecological environment under the State Council shall, together with the relevant departments under the State Council, formulate the total annual carbon emission allowances and the allocation plan, taking into account the factors such as economic and social development, industrial structure adjustment, industry development stage, historical emission situation, and market regulation needs, in accordance with the national greenhouse gas emission control targets, and shall organize their implementation. Carbon emission allowances shall be allocated free of charge, and the distribution method combining free and paid allocation shall be gradually implemented in accordance with the relevant requirements of the State.
The competent department of ecological environment of the provincial people's government shall, together with the relevant departments at the same level, issue carbon emission allowances to the key emitting entities within its administrative region in accordance with the total annual carbon emission allowances and the allocation plan, and shall not issue or adjust carbon emission allowances in violation of the total annual carbon emission allowances and the allocation plan.

Article 10 When studying and proposing the types of greenhouse gases and industry scopes covered by carbon emissions trading, formulating the conditions for determining key emitting entities, and the total annual carbon emission allowances and the allocation plan in accordance with Articles 6, 8, and 9 of these Regulations, opinions shall be solicited from provincial people's governments, relevant industry associations, enterprises and institutions, experts, and the public.

Article 11 Key emitting entities shall take effective measures to control greenhouse gas emissions, formulate and strictly implement a greenhouse gas emission data quality control plan in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State and the technical specifications formulated by the competent department of ecological environment under the State Council, use measuring instruments that have passed metrological verification or calibration according to law to conduct greenhouse gas emission-related inspection and testing, truthfully and accurately calculate and account for their own greenhouse gas emissions, prepare the greenhouse gas emission report for the preceding year (hereinafter referred to as the annual emission report), and submit the emission statistical accounting data and the annual emission report to the competent department of ecological environment of the provincial people's government where their production and business premises are located in accordance with the provisions.
Key emitting entities shall be responsible for the truthfulness, completeness, and accuracy of their emission statistical accounting data and annual emission report.
Key emitting entities shall disclose to the public information on their emissions, emission facilities, and statistical accounting methods in the annual emission report in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State. The original records and management ledgers of the data involved in the annual emission report shall be kept for at least five years.
Key emitting entities may entrust technical service institutions established according to law to conduct greenhouse gas emission-related inspection and testing and prepare annual emission reports.

Article 12 The competent department of ecological environment of the provincial people's government shall verify the annual emission report submitted by the key emitting entity to confirm its actual greenhouse gas emissions. The verification work shall be completed within the prescribed time limit, and the verification results shall be provided to the key emitting entity within seven working days from the date of completion of the verification. The verification results shall be disclosed to the public.
The competent department of ecological environment of the provincial people's government may, through means such as government purchase of services, entrust a technical service institution established according to law to conduct a technical review of the annual emission report. The key emitting entity shall cooperate with the technical service institution in conducting the technical review and provide the relevant data and materials truthfully.

Article 13 A technical service institution entrusted to conduct greenhouse gas emission-related inspection and testing shall comply with the relevant national technical regulations and technical specification requirements, bear corresponding responsibility for the inspection and testing reports it issues, and shall not issue untrue or false inspection and testing reports. Key emitting entities shall prepare and submit samples for testing in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State and be responsible for the representativeness and truthfulness of the samples.
A technical service institution entrusted to prepare annual emission reports or to conduct technical reviews of annual emission reports shall, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State, have the corresponding facilities and equipment, technical capabilities, and technical personnel, establish a business quality management system, and conduct relevant business independently, objectively, and impartially. It shall bear corresponding responsibility for the annual emission reports and technical review opinions it issues, and shall not tamper with or forge data materials, use false data materials, or engage in other acts of fraud. The specific management measures for the preparation and technical review of annual emission reports shall be formulated by the competent department of ecological environment under the State Council together with the relevant departments under the State Council.
A technical service institution shall not concurrently engage in both the annual emission report preparation business and the technical review business within the same province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government.

Article 14 Key emitting entities shall, based on the verification results of the annual emission report by the competent department of ecological environment of the provincial people's government, and within the time limit prescribed by the competent department of ecological environment under the State Council, fully surrender their carbon emission allowances.
Key emitting entities may purchase or sell carbon emission allowances through the national carbon emissions trading market, and the carbon emission allowances they purchase may be used for surrender.
Key emitting entities may, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State, purchase certified greenhouse gas emission reductions to be used for surrendering their carbon emission allowances.

Article 15 Carbon emissions trading may be conducted through negotiated transfer, unilateral bidding, or other spot trading methods that comply with the relevant provisions of the State.
No unit or individual shall manipulate the national carbon emissions trading market or disrupt the order of the national carbon emissions trading market by means of fraud, malicious collusion, dissemination of false information, or other means.

Article 16 The competent department of ecological environment under the State Council shall establish a national carbon emissions trading market management platform to strengthen the whole-process supervision and management of the allocation and surrender of carbon emission allowances and the greenhouse gas emissions of key emitting entities, and shall achieve information sharing with the relevant departments under the State Council.

Article 17 The competent department of ecological environment and other departments with supervisory and management responsibilities may conduct on-site inspections of transaction entities such as key emitting entities and technical service institutions within their respective scopes of duties.
When conducting on-site inspections, the competent department of ecological environment and other departments with supervisory and management responsibilities may take measures such as reviewing and copying relevant materials, inquiring into and inspecting relevant information systems, and may require relevant units and individuals to provide explanations on relevant matters. The party being inspected shall truthfully present the situation and provide materials, and shall not refuse or obstruct the inspection.
When conducting on-site inspections, the number of inspectors shall not be less than two, and they shall present their law enforcement credentials. Inspectors shall be obligated to keep confidential, according to law, the State secrets and trade secrets learned during the inspection.

Article 18 Any unit or individual has the right to report any act violating the provisions of these Regulations to the competent department of ecological environment and other departments with supervisory and management responsibilities. The department receiving the report shall handle it promptly according to law, provide feedback to the whistleblower on the handling results in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State, and keep the whistleblower's identity confidential.

Article 19 If a staff member of the competent department of ecological environment or other departments with supervisory and management responsibilities abuses their power, neglects their duties, or engages in malpractice for personal gain in the supervision and management of carbon emissions trading and related activities, they shall be given disciplinary sanctions according to law.

Article 20 If a staff member of the competent department of ecological environment, other departments with supervisory and management responsibilities, the national carbon emissions registration institution, the national carbon emissions trading institution, or a technical service institution specified in these Regulations participates in carbon emissions trading, the competent department of ecological environment under the State Council shall order the lawful disposal of the carbon emission allowances and other trading products held by the staff member, confiscate the illegal gains, and may also impose a fine of not more than the value of the carbon emission allowances and other products traded; if the staff member is a State functionary, disciplinary sanctions shall also be imposed according to law.

Article 23 If a technical service institution issues an untrue or false inspection and testing report, the competent department of ecological environment shall order it to make corrections, confiscate the illegal gains, and impose a fine of not less than five times but not more than ten times the illegal gains; if there are no illegal gains or the illegal gains are less than 20,000 yuan, a fine of not less than 20,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, the department responsible for qualification accreditation shall revoke its inspection and testing qualification.
If the annual emission report or technical review opinion issued by a technical service institution contains major defects or omissions, or data materials are tampered with or forged, false data materials are used, or other fraudulent acts are carried out during the preparation of the annual emission report or the technical review of the annual emission report, the competent department of ecological environment shall order it to make corrections, confiscate the illegal gains, and impose a fine of not less than five times but not more than ten times the illegal gains; if there are no illegal gains or the illegal gains are less than 200,000 yuan, a fine of not less than 200,000 yuan but not more than 1 million yuan shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, it shall be prohibited from engaging in the preparation and technical review of annual emission reports.
If a technical service institution is penalized for the illegal acts specified in the first and second paragraphs of this Article, a fine of not less than 20,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan shall be imposed on its directly responsible person in charge and other directly responsible persons, and they shall be prohibited from engaging in greenhouse gas emission-related inspection and testing, annual emission report preparation, and technical review for five years; if the circumstances are serious, they shall be prohibited from engaging in the aforementioned business for life.

Article 24 If a key emitting entity fails to surrender its carbon emission allowances in accordance with the provisions, the competent department of ecological environment shall order it to make corrections and impose a fine of not less than five times but not more than ten times the average market transaction price in the month before the surrender deadline for the unsurfendered carbon emission allowances; if it refuses to make corrections, its carbon emission allowances for the following year shall be reduced by an amount equal to the unsurfendered carbon emission allowances, and it may be ordered to suspend production for rectification.

Article 25 If a party manipulates the national carbon emissions trading market, the competent department of ecological environment under the State Council shall order it to make corrections, confiscate the illegal gains, and impose a fine of not less than one time but not more than ten times the illegal gains; if there are no illegal gains or the illegal gains are less than 500,000 yuan, a fine of not less than 500,000 yuan but not more than 5 million yuan shall be imposed. If a unit is penalized for the aforementioned illegal acts, a warning shall be given to its directly responsible person in charge and other directly responsible persons, and a fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 1 million yuan shall be imposed.
If a party disrupts the order of the national carbon emissions trading market, the competent department of ecological environment under the State Council shall order it to make corrections, confiscate the illegal gains, and impose a fine of not less than one time but not more than ten times the illegal gains; if there are no illegal gains or the illegal gains are less than 100,000 yuan, a fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 1 million yuan shall be imposed. If a unit is penalized for the aforementioned illegal acts, a warning shall be given to its directly responsible person in charge and other directly responsible persons, and a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan shall be imposed.

Article 26 If a party refuses or obstructs the competent department of ecological environment or other departments with supervisory and management responsibilities from carrying out supervision and inspection according to law, the competent department of ecological environment or other departments with supervisory and management responsibilities shall order it to make corrections and impose a fine of not less than 20,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan.

Article 27 The competent department of ecological environment under the State Council shall, together with the relevant departments under the State Council, establish a credit record system for transaction entities such as key emitting entities and technical service institutions, and shall incorporate information on administrative penalties imposed on transaction entities such as key emitting entities and technical service institutions for violating the provisions of these Regulations into the relevant national credit information system, and shall disclose such information to the public according to law.

Article 28 Any party that violates the provisions of these Regulations and causes damage to others shall bear civil liability according to law; if the act constitutes a violation of public security administration, a public security administration penalty shall be imposed according to law; if the act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 29 For local carbon emissions trading markets established prior to the coming into force of these Regulations, the relevant management systems shall be improved and strengthened by reference to the provisions of these Regulations.
After these Regulations come into force, no new local carbon emissions trading markets shall be established, and key emitting entities shall no longer participate in carbon emissions trading in local carbon emissions trading markets covering the same types of greenhouse gases and the same industries.

Article 30 For the purposes of these Regulations, the following terms have the meanings ascribed to them:
(1) "Greenhouse gases" means the natural and anthropogenic gaseous constituents of the atmosphere that absorb and re-emit infrared radiation, including carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, hydrofluorocarbons, perfluorocarbons, sulfur hexafluoride, and nitrogen trifluoride.
(2) "Carbon emission allowances" means the emission quotas for greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide allocated to key emitting entities for a specified period. One unit of carbon emission allowance is equivalent to one ton of carbon dioxide equivalent emitted into the atmosphere.
(3) "Surrender" means the act by which a key emitting entity delivers to the competent department of ecological environment, within the prescribed time limit, carbon emission allowances equal to its verified actual greenhouse gas emissions for the preceding year.

Article 31 If a key emitting entity consumes non-fossil energy electricity, its carbon emission allowances and greenhouse gas emissions shall be adjusted accordingly in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.

Article 32 The competent department of ecological environment under the State Council may, together with the competent departments for civil aviation and other relevant departments under the State Council, in accordance with the principles stipulated in these Regulations, based on actual needs and taking into account the characteristics of greenhouse gas emission control in industries such as civil aviation, formulate specific management measures for matters such as the formulation of the list of key emitting entities in industries such as civil aviation, the issuance and surrender of carbon emission allowances, the statistical calculation and accounting of greenhouse gas emission data, and the submission and verification of annual emission reports.
Article 33 These Regulations shall come into force as of May 1, 2024.
